text.p: Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet on Monday lifted price controls on goods in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to speed up the transition to a market economy.
"With the decree approved by the cabinet today, prices on all goods are liberalised," a government spokeswoman told reporters.
Profit margins remain in force for nine items, including tap water, railway tickets and basic foods like milk, bread, cooking oil, cheese, yoghurt and salami, said the spokeswoman.
The decree takes effect from the date of publication in the State Gazette, expected on Friday.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the IMF, Bulgaria pledged to stabilise its financial system through the introduction of a self-regulating monetary mechanism, known as a currency board. Other pledges include liberalising prices to offset possible food or fuel shortages and boost agricultural production.

In a move to boost the domestic farm market the cabinet has already lifted farm produce export bans with effect from July 1 and announced that prices of agricultural products will be market-determined.
